result_text:
The per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`java`, `js`, `xml`), and landscapes merge old `"  *.java"` data with new `"java"` data under one entry. The codeanalyzer (330 tests) and reports suites pass. Nothing is committed.

What changed:

- **Naming** (`SourceCodeAspectUtils.java`): per-extension aspects are created as `extension`, not `"  *." + extension`.
- **Metrics and summary** (`AnalysisUtils.java`): `NUMBER_OF_FILES_…_EXT_JAVA` and `LINES_OF_CODE_…_EXT_JAVA` ids are unchanged (`getMetricId` produces the same upper-cased id). The indented text-summary lines still read `  *.java: N files…`, because I kept the look there.
- **Landscape aggregation** (`LandscapeAnalysisResults.java`): a new `getBareExtension` helper strips `*.`, trims and lower-cases names. It is applied both in the per-repository aggregation and in the `merge` of build/generated/other, so the main scope and the merged "other" category each produce one entry per language. Each merged entry still lists every contributing repository.
- **Report code**: I removed the `replace("*.", "")` strips on per-extension names in nine report files (`ReportFileExporter`, `SummaryUtils`, `OverviewReportGenerator`, the landscape report generators, `LandscapeVisualsGenerator`, and the landscape data/repository exporters). These were no-ops on bare names. The `CommitsPerExtension.getExtension()` strips are untouched.
- **Tests**: `CodeConfigurationTest` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` now assert `java`/`js`/`html`.

Two things to know:

- The permission layer blocked a single `perl -pi` substitution, so I made those report edits one by one with the Edit tool. The result is the same.
- The mixed old/new landscape merge is verified by reading the code, not by a new test; no existing test covers it. The code browser's scope list will now show `java` where it showed `  *.java`.
